MY LITTLE SCIENCE PROJECT

How Tall Is Your Plant?

Once your seedling is planted in soil, measure its height and compare your records.

Stand a ruler beside the plant with zero at the soil surface. Read the height at the highest point without pulling or stretching the plant. Use the same method each time. A grown-up can help you subtract an earlier height from a later height.

With a grown-up: use untreated planting beans; do not eat seeds or sprouts. Keep small seeds away from younger children. Wash hands after handling. An adult should discard any mouldy setup.

LOOK · THINK · TRY

Explore before you start.

A fair comparison uses the same unit and starting point. Plants may grow at different rates, and small differences can also come from how we measure.

Look at the picture, talk about what you notice, then use the drawing and writing spaces below. Open the picture for a closer look.

Choose one method

Keep the ruler upright, with zero at the soil surface. Measure to the same part of the plant each time without stretching it.

Compare two records

Subtract an earlier height from a later height to find the change. If your plant was 4 cm and is now 6 cm, the difference is 2 cm.

A surprising result

A drooping leaf or a tilted ruler can change a reading. Check your method before deciding that the plant became shorter.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

Measurement one

Measure from the soil surface to the highest point of your plant.

ACTIVITY 2

Measurement two

Measure again another day, using the same starting point and centimetres.

ACTIVITY 3

Measurement three

Compare your latest measurement with your earlier records.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

A fair comparison uses the same unit and starting point. Plants may grow at different rates, and small differences can also come from how we measure.
